chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: T Town Blues, the 1980 tribute and the 1939 Hammond sessions
summary: A singer revives T Town Blues the night Count Basie honours Fields in Tulsa; the 1939 Hammond sessions did not get the push they deserved.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now, in 1980, I have a write-up there, that some lady--I'm going to give it to you, Preston--I had some run off, Count happened to be in town that night, and of course, he had produced and said that he kind of looked on Tulsa as his second home and blah, blah, blah, and to be with his friend Ernie Fields for a while, and then that same night, that same night, a young lady did T Town Blues, in Norfolk, Virginia, I believe it was, and it was in the paper. Somebody took it out and says Ernie Fields, Sr. was recognized at the Count Basie concert and also the same night a young lady did T Town Blues, and it was sensational,

in Norfolk, Virginia, on a blue concert, and everybody wanted to know--nobody had ever heard of her before. And so she announced, I don't know what, but Ernie Fields band did this years ago. What I'm fixing to say is, that it was one of the biggest things we did in thirty nine, but it looked like for some reason they just didn't give it the push that they should have.

I won't blame it all on Hammond; we did two sessions for Hammond in 1939, but I had left--I had a little mishap when I was in New York. Before we left there, we'll get to that, but since we're talking about Melvin, I'd like to say it right now because Melvin was featured on both sessions.
